headline: Australia's coach admits Bangladesh wins first Test in Australia
summary: Coach Andrew McDonald admits the team failed to maintain standards after a dominant performance by Bangladesh in Darwin.
details: Bangladesh has achieved a historic first Test victory on Australian soil in Darwin, dominating the match throughout the last three and a half days.
Australia was bowled out for 198 in their first innings, trailing Bangladesh by 226 runs. In their second innings, they could only set a target of 57 runs for Bangladesh.
Bangladesh reached the target, losing only one wicket to secure the win. The result has put significant pressure on the Australian team and coaching staff.
Australian head coach Andrew McDonald admitted the team played poorly, stating that scoring under 500 runs across two innings on such a wicket was a failure to maintain their standards.
Former cricketer Ricky Ponting has called for immediate changes to Australia's opening and number three positions, suggesting a need to for the new generation of players.
McDonald noted that while calls for change are easy to make, the current players still have a lot of cricket ahead of them, though team balance and age will remain under discussion.
caption:
A historic first! Bangladesh secures a stunning Test win in Australia, leaving the Australian coach admitting they failed their own standards.

Bangladesh has achieved a historic first Test victory on Australian soil in Darwin, dominating the match throughout the last three and a half days.

Australia was bowled out for 198 in their first innings, trailing Bangladesh by 226 runs. In their second innings, they could only set a target of 57 runs for Bangladesh.

Bangladesh reached the target, losing only one wicket to secure the win. The result has put significant pressure on the Australian team and coaching staff.

Australian head coach Andrew McDonald admitted the team played poorly, stating that scoring under 500 runs across two innings on such a wicket was a failure to maintain their standards.

Former cricketer Ricky Ponting has called for immediate changes to Australia's opening and number three positions, suggesting a need to for the new generation of players.

McDonald noted that while calls for change are easy to make, the current players still have a lot of cricket ahead of them, though team balance and age will remain under discussion.

headline: Cabinet approves draft to abolish RAB and form SRB
summary: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a specialized unit under the police force.
details: The cabinet has given final approval to the draft 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026', pending vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.
Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), which will operate as a specialized unit under the police force.
The approved draft includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to handle complaints from citizens and internal conflicts among unit members.
All personnel, orders, powers, funds, assets, and records currently associated with RAB will be transferred to the SRB.
Until new rules are formulated, existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations.
caption:
RAB is set to be abolished. A new specialized police unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will take its place.

The cabinet has given final approval to the draft 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026', pending vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.

Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), which will operate as a specialized unit under the police force.

The approved draft includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to handle complaints from citizens and internal conflicts among unit members.

All personnel, orders, powers, funds, assets, and records currently associated with RAB will be transferred to the SRB.

Until new rules are formulated, existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
